stem.text: An alkene reacts with hot, concentrated, acidified potassium manganate(VII) to produce a single organic product as shown.

stem.alt: Reaction scheme: alkene, with hot, concentrated, acidified KMnO4(aq), gives a single organic product drawn as a skeletal formula containing two C=O groups and a terminal -OH (carboxylic acid) group

stem.text: What is the structure of the alkene?

A.alt: Skeletal formula: six-membered ring containing a C=C double bond, with a methyl group on one alkene carbon and a methyl group on another ring carbon

B.alt: Skeletal formula: six-membered ring containing a C=C double bond, with a methyl group on one alkene carbon and a methyl group on the adjacent ring carbon

C.alt: Skeletal formula: five-membered ring containing a C=C double bond, with a methyl group on one alkene carbon and a methyl group on the ring carbon next to the other alkene carbon

D.alt: Skeletal formula: five-membered ring containing a C=C double bond, with a methyl group on one alkene carbon and a methyl group on the adjacent ring carbon
